newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU to send Irish minister on Mideast peace mission.
newsitem.headline: EU to send Irish minister on Mideast peace mission.

text.p: The European Union, frustrated by being left out of U.S.-brokered Middle East peace moves, decided on Saturday to send Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring on a peace mission to meet both Palestinians and Israelis.

Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, whose government holds the EU presidency, said Spring would leave "at the earliest possible time in the coming week" to help the Middle East peace process. Irish officials said he would leave in three or four days.

Bruton said EU leaders meeting in Dublin had also discussed the appointment of a special envoy to the region, who would ensure a longer-term EU involvement in Middle East affairs. He said the envoy would probably concentrate on economic issues.

The EU has been frustrated by its exclusion from U.S. Middle East peace moves and Bruton said it was appropriate that Europe should have a significant role, particularly since it is by far the largest donor of humanitarian and development aid in support of the peace process.

The EU last Tuesday issued a tough statement calling on Israel to match its stated desire for peace with actions to fulfil its obligations. The statement criticised the use of tanks and helicopter gunships in the unrest.
Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said it was clear that Israel had been unhappy with the statement.
"That put us in a very difficult and uncomfortable situation," he added.

Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat appealed this week for more EU involvement in efforts to patch up the peace process. But some EU officials in Dublin said the U.S. appeared unenthusiastic about a greater European role.
Diplomats said they had been told that U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher had sent a letter to the EU which appeared to suggest it should not become too involved in the current peace effort.
Spring said the EU had made it clear it wanted to play a part. "We have had a dialogue with the U.S. this week. They know we want to be involved," he told Irish RTE television.

Israel and the Palestinian Authority hold talks on the Israeli border on Sunday. They are expected to discuss the closure of an archeological tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem whose opening sparked violence which killed 73 people.

Asked whether Spring would press for the closure of the tunnel, or make a potentially controversial visit to the Palestinian Authority's Orient House offices in disputed East Jerusalem, Bruton said details had not yet been decided.
Israel has already signalled that it would strongly disapprove of any visit by the EU to Orient House, which it would see as backing for Palestinian claims to East Jerusalem.

It has raised the possibility that it would refuse to meet EU representatives if they also visited Orient House. Spring paid a visit to Orient House in 1995 and was promptly snubbed by the Israeli president, who cancelled planned talks.
But Bruton said he believed Spring would be welcomed by both sides during this visit. "I am sure the initiative will be well- received by the parties concerned," he said.
The EU had been planning to send a "troika" of ministers to the Middle East in mid-October, but this may be deferred because of Spring's visit, EU officials said.
French President Jacques Chirac, who had been pressing the summit to reaffirm Europe's desire to play a role in rescuing the peace process, said the EU would be even-handed.
"It is not a question for the EU to be for one or for the other," he said. "It is for peace."
"Security for Israel depends on peace. Peace depends on negotiation," Chirac said.
